title: Recognition or Individuation? A Non-Additive Claim Against an Additive One
voice: agent-drafted under owner direction; not human-reviewed

claims.text: The passage names the discernment (viveka) by which a person rises above māyā.
On the formalised Trika side, recognition lands on what is already present and adds no new content (theorem paraphrase, not a reading).
On the Jungian side, individuation integrates the Self, so the endpoint is achieved rather than merely uncovered.
If the two accounts differ on additivity, they should differ clinically: uncovering versus constructing.
Settling condition: a durable change with no new content delivered and none needed, or an additive intervention matching recognition outcomes.

open_questions: Is the Jungian 'Self' an addition or a disclosure under another name?
Does either account make a different prediction a clinician could observe?
